purpose: Apply the supplied reversal, linear-stability, and material-response ideas inside matched SIMS experiments, alongside analytic and numerical checks.
model_status: An explicit continuous-state SIMS extension. The original binary copying experiment retains its original rules and results. These response rules are chosen hypotheses, not fitted participant behavior.
weights: Undirected adjacency divided by each graph's maximum degree; L = diag(row sums) - W. Symmetric contact weights conserve the population mean under pure alignment.
initial_states: For each start, draw two coordinates per SIM uniformly on [-0.6,0.6], then subtract each population-coordinate mean and add (0.1,-0.04). Reuse the resulting state across all graphs and conditions. Reversal and rate experiments use its first coordinate.
linear_rule: Yprime = Y A^T - 2 L Y. A is one of the seven saved reference matrices. Each SIM has an expressed preference displacement and a response coordinate. Both coordinates exchange with neighbors. Compute exact finite-time evolution from graph modes and the 2x2 exponential.
reversal_rule: xprime = -(2 I + W) cos(x). The two-SIM one-edge reduction is the supplied textbook equation. The sum of sin(x_i) decreases under forward evolution. One intervention reverses the sign of the rule from time 2 through 4, then restores it.
rate_rule: xprime = q signal(t) 1 - r (I + 2 L) x. Signal is +1 before time 4 and -1 thereafter. r=(mu/rho)/(mu_H/rho_H). Fixed-input q=rho_H/rho; target-matched q=r. Values come from the saved 25 C material-property controls and serve as dimensionless response sensitivities for SIMS.
measurements: RMS spread of participant state vectors around their population mean; norm of the population mean; fraction with positive preference beyond 0.02; choice unanimity only if every first coordinate exceeds +0.02 or every coordinate is below -0.02; first and final sampled unanimity and sampled breaks. Rate settling requires every SIM to remain within 5% of the final target for the rest of the recorded window, with at least one unit of confirmation after the input switch.
numerical_controls: Exact two-SIM reductions; independent RK4 comparison for the coupled linear and rate equations; permutation and graph-mode invariants; reversal step halving for three starts per graph and both conditions. Record all outcomes, including unset settling times.
interpretation: Agreement of coordinates, agreement of choices, and attraction to a bounded state are different measurements. Time is dimensionless. Property ratios choose alternative response rules; the SIMS are not physical water molecules. Sampling intervals over matched starts describe the chosen initial-state distribution only.
